thread:
Maria: Quick heads-up — after the commit that changed kernel routing heuristics, we're seeing HBM RW bandwidth peg on some long-seq jobs (seqlen ~ 2048) and KV cache churn. Attaching initial nsys dump soon.
Noah: ugh, timeline? any obvious kernels?
Maria: Uploading nsys: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx -o run_maria_2048 ./serve --workload=longseq` -> timeline looks like repeated small memcpy + matmul fallback spikes. HBM bandwidth spikes to ~680GB/s for several seconds, then drops.
Kevin: Is this the change that prefers fused-attn when seqlen < 1024 and falls back after threshold? Could be mis-classifying long chunks.
Chris: I grabbed a perfetto slice. The KV cache eviction events correlate with the bandwidth spikes. When cache misses rise, we see microbatching increase and DMA bursts.
Sara: Any binder-level logs? kernel selection logs?
Maria: yes — pinging sample log snippet: ```[2026-03-12T14:22:11Z] kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_v2 fallback_reason=large_kv_span estimated_seq=1984 batch=8``` 
Lina: That looked like the decision heuristic using an old seq-estimator. We changed the estimator weights in 8d9c2f3 — maybe off by factor for windowed KV spans.
Noah: I ran a smaller repro with nvprof and got heavy L2 read/write counters during the spikes. NVPROF snippet: ```GPU activities: HtoD copies: 3.2GB, Device memory throughput: 650GB/s, DRAM read: 92%```
Kevin: So it's not purely compute-bound, it's memory streaming. Probably KV cache prefetch is issuing large ranges and causing interleaved DMA thrash.
Chris: Perfetto shows periodic full-KV-scan at ~50ms intervals; looks like prefetch window grows and stops being selective.
Sara: Could this be triggered by large prompt tokens being split across microbatches? Batching heuristic might increase prefetch lookahead.
Maria: Repro steps I used: `./serve --seqlen=2048 --model=mpt-35b --batcher=continuous --kv_cache=enabled` then run nsys. I can share the nsys file.
Noah: Can you also capture `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` and the kernel names/timings? Need to see where matmul_v2 vs fused-attn vs matmul_v1 are used.
Maria: attached `run_maria_2048.qdrep` and a short perfetto URL.
Lina: Quick grep in logs shows a new codepath: `if estimated_seq > seq_thresh_v2` but seq_thresh_v2 set to 1500 in config — seems right. But estimator returns 1984 due to counting extra prompt tokens from metadata.
Kevin: That would flip kernel selection into a less-optimal matmul path at runtime. matmul_v2 has worse HBM locality for our attention implementation -> more streaming.
Chris: Proposed mitigation: clamp estimated_seq to actual request_seq and add a safety cap for prefetch window. Also add hysteresis to kernel switching to avoid flip-flopping per-microbatch.
Sara: For immediate stopgap: reduce continuous batch max_batch_size from 16 to 8 for longseq tenants and reduce prefetch window to 32KB. Should reduce DMA bursts.
Noah: I'll run a quick A/B: baseline commit vs candidate patch that clamps seq estimator.
perf-bot: perf-run queued: run_id=5234 baseline=main candidate=clamp-seq-estimator
Maria: After a local patch (clamp_seq_estimator + hysteresis=2), re-ran nsys: bandwidth peaks fell to ~320GB/s, KV miss rate down 60%, latency P95 improved ~20%.
Kevin: Nice. But longer-term we should tweak kernel selection weights so fused-attn stays chosen for the observed access pattern. Maybe add a feature: use recent KV hit/miss ratio as an input to kernel selector.
Lina: Agree. Also note that quantized matmul path behaves differently — for int8 path we saw lower bandwidth but higher compute jitter; need separate thresholds.
Chris: Can we add an NVTX span around KV prefetch and kernel selection decision so future nsys traces annotate the decision moment?
Maria: Done locally. Example NVTX markers: ```nvtxRangePushA(\"kv:prefetch:start\"); ... nvtxRangePop(); nvtxRangePushA(\"kernel-select:begin\");```
Noah: Summary of next steps: 1) Patch clamp + hysteresis (short-term) 2) Add NVTX spans + counters (observability) 3) Tune kernel selection model to include KV miss ratio + quant path 4) Adjust batching defaults for longseq (prod rollout controlled)
Sara: For rollout, prefer a canary with 1% traffic on Dedicated nodes, monitor HBM BW and KV miss. If stable, ramp to 25% then 100%.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy initiated: canary=1% nodeset=dedicated-longseq-1 commit=clamp-seq-estimator
Maria: Also leaving a note: the perf regression surfaced after commit 8d9c2f3 and we should mark that in the regression tracker. I'll open a small postmortem once we've stabilized.
Kevin: Did we check if the same pattern shows on A100 vs H100? Memory controller differences could change thresholds.
Maria: Good call — initial runs were on H100. Noah, can you run the same patch on A100?
Noah: Running now, will post nvprof + nsys in thread.
Lina: I'll start a small patch to add KV hit ratio into kernel_selector model, PR inbound in 30m.
Chris: For long-term, we should add an offline benchmark that stress-tests KV prefetch + high seqlen to detect regressions automatically on PRs.
Sara: Agreed — create a CI perf job that runs a 2-minute nsys trace and checks HBM BW threshold and KV miss counts.
Maria: Thanks all. Uploading perf artifacts and the quick repro script in the thread attachments. Will follow up with a short blameless postmortem. :thumbsup:
Noah: nvprof/A100 results: bandwidth slightly lower but still peaky; seems heuristics still needed. I'll add to the PR.
Lina: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/3452 kernel_selector: add kv_miss_ratio feature
Maria: Closing loop — after canary ramp to 25% we saw no further HBM saturations for 6h window. Marking issue as mitigated pending kernel selector improvements.
Sara: Thanks!"
